title: Aphasia Profile Comparator
summary: Six fictional language profiles on six original measures - fluency of spontaneous speech, understanding, repetition, naming, reading aloud and writing. The learner puts any two side by side, predicts which single measure does most to separate them, and is marked against the arithmetic. One profile fits no textbook pattern, which is the subject of the challenge.
learningObjectives: Identify which measure carries the most information about a particular contrast.
Explain why repetition is disproportionately informative, and what a disproportionate difficulty or sparing implies.
Recognise when two measures separate a pair so nearly equally that the largest gap is not a useful answer.
Explain why the classical categories fit a substantial minority of people badly.
State why a language profile constrains the processing more tightly than it constrains the anatomy.
interactionTypes: prediction of the most separating measure
privacy: No data collected, stored or transmitted; everything runs in the browser tab, and the tool asks nothing about the person using it.
accessibilityNotes: Native select, radio and button controls. The paired bar chart is hidden from assistive technology and paired with a visible table giving each measure, what it asks for, both scores and the separation, with the largest separation named in words in its own cell. The two profiles are distinguished by fill and by the profile letter printed at the start of each bar, and every bar prints its own score, so nothing depends on hue. A second table gives all six profiles on all six measures with the selected pair marked. The chart is pinned at 358px so both profiles stay visible while the measure radios at the bottom of the control column are used. Selecting a pair and checking a choice both announce through the shell's polite live region. Wide tables scroll inside their own containers, heading levels do not skip, reduced motion and forced colours are handled, and the layout is usable at 320px and at classroom-projector widths.
readmeTopic: Which piece of language evidence separates two profiles, why repetition is disproportionately informative, and why the classical categories are prototypes
simulationNotes: Six invented profiles on six invented measures, scored 0 to 10 where 10 is performance indistinguishable from a fictional control group. The separation between two profiles on a measure is the absolute difference between their scores, and the most informative measure for a pair is the one with the largest separation; measures within one point of the largest are reported as a near tie, because the largest gap stops being a useful answer at that point. Reference pairs - profile A against profile D is separated by repetition alone, by five points, with every other separation one point or less; profile A against profile B has fluency at seven and understanding at six, a near tie; profile C against profile D has repetition at six and fluency at five; profile B against profile C is separated by understanding, by six. Profile F fits no textbook pattern deliberately. Deliberate simplifications: six measures is a caricature, since real assessment separates single-word from sentence comprehension, word from non-word repetition and regular from irregular reading; fluency in particular bundles rate, phrase length, effort, articulation, grammatical structure and information content into one number. No standardised battery, subtest or item is reproduced, the task descriptions are original, no syndrome is named anywhere, no real person or published case appears, and nothing on the page assesses or diagnoses anybody.
